text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A go-slow by the meteorological department staff ends after the government pledges to address their grievances by the end of next month.
- The crisis in the opposition party FORD-Kenya deepens as faction leader Raila Odinga and member Chris Bichage refuse to attend disciplinary committee proceedings scheduled for Tuesday.
- More than 70 dairy farmers in Uasin Gishu and Nandi districts of the Rirt Valley accuse the giant Kenya Cooperative Creameries of giving them cheques which bounced for a third time.
- Agriculture Minister Simeon Nyachae dismisses as fictitious, claims there is bad blood between him and Vice-President George Saitoti.
- Hell breaks loose at Egerton university in Nakuru on Monday night as contingents of anti-riot police engage more than 7,000 rioting students in running battles.
- A patient dies instantly after jumping from the 10th floor of Kenyatta National Hospital in Nairobi.
- President Daniel arap Moi asks warring parties to the Great Lakes conflict to exercise restraint and create conditions to enable them to live together in harmony.
- Besieged FORD-Kenya faction leader Raila Odinga says that he will announce his official political stand on Friday.
- A senior clerical officer attached to the Rift Valley Provincial offices appears before a court facing charges of using the president's signature to defraud a Nakuru businessman.
